newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Financial reform proposals hit S.Korea bank shrs.
newsitem.headline: Financial reform proposals hit S.Korea bank shrs.

text.p: Shares in South Korean banks fell on Monday as investors showed their disappoinment at the government's final proposals to modernise the country's backward financial industry, brokers said.
The banking sub-index had dropped 8.50 points or 1.95 percent to 426.52 at 0230 GMT.
Kim Myong-ho at Hyundai Securities said investors had wanted the government to raise the individual bank ownership ceiling to 10 percent from the current four percent.
But the government proposals fell short of the market's anticipation.

Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik said at a news conference the ministry would accept most proposals presented by the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform. He said the central bank governor would be asked to set an annual inflation target and would be held responsible for meeting it.
